articles.summary: Bank Rakyat's corporate portal was defaced on 7 November, with a hacker alleging access to internal systems and stolen sample data. The bank only acknowledged a temporary access disruption and pointed customers to other channels. The minister later described the incident as a website defacement on a third-party-managed site. The data-theft claims remain unverified.
articles.title: A sign of escalating cyberattack in Malaysia after Bank Rakyat becomes latest victim of hacking?

articles.summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on 14 November that Malaysia faces thousands of attempted cyberattacks every month, linking the warning to efforts to strengthen the armed forces' cyber unit. It follows his 3 November remarks that the country is a likely target and comes as the national threat level sits at Medium.
articles.title: Malaysia faces thousands of attempted cyberattacks monthly, says Anwar

articles.summary: Tabung Haji suspended services after detecting suspicious cyber activity around 7 October, lodged a police report and notified NACSA and the personal data regulator. By 12 October key systems had resumed and depositors' savings were confirmed safe, though some functions stayed limited. It is among the incidents behind the November threat-level rise.
articles.title: Tabung Haji systems resume after cyberattack, depositors' savings confirmed safe

articles.summary: The Election Commission said on 10 November that its website appeared to be under cyberattack and that it was working with MCMC to protect it. Chairman Ramlan Harun said an initial report was filed. The extent of any intrusion has not been established, and the timing is close to the Melaka state election.
articles.title: EC, MCMC take measures to protect website following reported cyber attack

articles.summary: The health ministry said an unauthorised party accessed a file storage and sharing platform at one unnamed facility on Thursday 12 November. It says main databases and operational systems were untouched, blocked public access, reset passwords, audited servers and enforced multi-factor authentication, and warned the public against possessing or sharing leaked official documents.
articles.title: Health ministry suffers cybersecurity breach, but patient services not affected

articles.summary: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 12 November that NACSA remains at amber alert, a moderate readiness level. Claims of attacks and intrusions are circulating online, but NACSA has confirmed none so far and will be the official source of information.
articles.title: Nacsa maintains amber alert amid cyberattack, security breach claims

articles.summary: Extortion group n0n claims it stole close to a billion Expedia-related records, including loyalty data, traveller profiles and credentials, plus source code. Expedia confirmed attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider in a supply-chain attack, but has not verified the group's figures. Its investigation is ongoing and the numbers remain alleged.
articles.title: Extortion Group Claims Theft of Nearly One Billion Expedia Traveler Records

articles.summary: Maersk disclosed a breach of a legacy system at a logistics firm it acquired in 2022, after the WhiteArmor ransomware group demanded $5 million within 30 days and threatened to leak about 100GB. The company says no sensitive data was disclosed and no operational disruption is expected. Maersk is a key customer of Malaysian ports.
articles.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft Amid $5 Million Extortion Attempt

articles.summary: Vanderbilt University confirmed a cyber incident affecting campus devices, systems and cloud services, with the BYOD ransomware group claiming data theft. The university has not said whether data was taken. The same group was linked to the earlier Michigan State incident and a recent hospital attack.
articles.title: Vanderbilt University hit in BYOD ransomware attack, data theft claimed

articles.summary: Researchers described 'Operation Snowball', in which an unknown Chinese-speaking actor used an autonomous AI framework to exploit Cisco BroadWorks at a European telecom and 13 hosted firms. Over two weeks it enumerated hundreds of assets and exfiltrated subscriber billing and device records. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 10 November.
articles.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches

articles.summary: Binarly found that attacks compromising almost 1,000 Zyxel GS1900 switches used an unknown zero-day, not the previously patched flaw blamed by GreyNoise. Attackers deployed Jitterly and Sixzut malware variants. Zyxel released fixes on 23 October and published its advisory on 3 November.
articles.title: Zyxel Switch Hacks Blamed on Patched Flaw Actually Exploited a Zero-Day

articles.summary: On 9 November Paris prosecutors and ANSSI attributed the 12 October attack on about 700 French supermarkets to the IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh group. Refrigeration reached 50C for hours. France summoned the Iranian ambassador and promised EU sanctions, and similar incidents were reported in several other European countries.
articles.title: France Blames Iran for a Cyberattack That Heated Supermarket Refrigerators

milestones.label: Melaka special public holiday after state election

articles.summary: Ab Rauf Yusoh was sworn in on 15 November as Melaka's 13th Chief Minister for a second term, a day after the state election. Reports put BN at 21 of 28 seats, PN at three and PH at four, with BN and PN nominating him. He declared Monday a special public holiday.
articles.title: Ab Rauf sworn in for second term as Melaka Chief Minister

articles.summary: Anwar said the Attorney General has asked for an audience with the King to explain the house arrest issue involving Najib Razak. He added that the AG faced constraints because the matter is tied to the separate 1MDB case. The dispute over the royal addendum and the Pardons Board continues.
articles.title: AG seeks audience with King to clarify Najib's house arrest issue, says Anwar

articles.summary: The Court of Appeal heard the federal government's challenge to parts of the High Court ruling on Sabah's 40% net revenue entitlement for 1974 to 2021 and reserved its decision. Case management was fixed for 12 November. The federal government holds a stay of the review order pending the appeal; the outcome of 12 November was not reported.
articles.title: Appellate court reserves decision on Sabah's 40% revenue entitlement appeal

articles.summary: Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution told the Dewan Rakyat on 12 November that a breach of house-arrest conditions would revoke the order and return Najib to Kajang Prison. Three prison officers per shift guard the residence at no extra cost, drawn from Kajang Prison staff.
articles.title: Najib could go back to prison if he breaches terms of house arrest, Dewan Rakyat told

articles.summary: A three-judge Court of Appeal bench unanimously set aside a High Court ruling and allowed 1MDB and related companies to file a 319-page affidavit supporting their Mareva injunction bid against Rosmah Mansor. The court said the High Court wrongly required exceptional circumstances. The ruling affects evidence only and does not itself freeze any assets.
articles.title: Court of Appeal allows 1MDB to use Singaporean woman's affidavit in bid to freeze Rosmah's RM1.41b assets

milestones.label: Federal Court hears IRB leave bid over Najib bankruptcy stay

articles.summary: The Federal Court will hear the Inland Revenue Board's leave application on 23 February 2027, challenging the Court of Appeal's September stay of bankruptcy proceedings against Najib Razak over a RM1.69 billion tax claim. The board has filed no similar application for Najib's son Nazifuddin, whose proceedings also remain stayed pending tax appeals.
articles.title: IRB's RM1.69b appeal in Najib bankruptcy case set for Feb 23; no appeal for Nazifuddin

articles.summary: Business Today summarises Parliament's sixth week: the house-arrest terms barring Najib from leaving the premises, politics and media, plus debate on national debt and GST. House arrest runs to 23 August 2028, and the Bar has sought judicial review of the Pardons Board decision.
articles.title: Najib House Arrest Conditions, National Debt And GST Dominate Parliament's Sixth Week

response.text: Push the Chrome update and a relaunch deadline through your MDM or browser management policy instead of building custom automation. Report compliance from the console and have XSOAR only open a ticket for non-compliant hosts. This is faster and safer than scripted installs.

response.prompt: Summarise CVE-2026-125350 (Chrome XML use-after-free, exploited in the wild, KEV due 2026-11-24) for non-technical managers in under 120 words. Include fixed Chrome 157 builds, who must update, and how to verify browser version. Do not speculate about attackers beyond what is public.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to summarise exposure for this exploited browser flaw in plain language. The analyst gets a short note listing affected versions, patch steps and the KEV deadline for management. Review the draft before sending.

response.text: Schedule a daily job that runs an XQL query over endpoint software inventory for Chrome versions below 157.0.8103.50. It posts the count and top affected hosts to the incident channel until the figure reaches zero. Stop the job after the KEV deadline passes.
response.title: Daily unpatched-browser report

articles.summary: Google patched a use-after-free in Chrome's XML component that is exploited in the wild, the eighth Chrome zero-day this year. An anonymous researcher reported it on 6 November. CISA added it to KEV on 10 November, so browsers on analyst and staff endpoints need updating quickly.

response.title: Hunt query drafting

response.text: Where patching is delayed, restrict access to the BroadWorks OCI interface to known management networks on your NGFW instead of building monitoring first. This removes the unauthenticated attack path immediately. Use XSIAM only to alert on blocked attempts.
response.title: Restrict OCI exposure at firewall

articles.summary: An XXE flaw in the BroadWorks Open Client Interface lets an unauthenticated attacker read sensitive configuration data. It was used in 'Operation Snowball' against a European telecom, with the actor recovering private keys and credentials. CISA added it to KEV on 10 November, although Cisco patched it months earlier.

response.text: Disable internet-facing HTTP management on switches and limit it to a management VLAN or jump host. This cuts off the unauthenticated attack path today, before firmware is upgraded. Verify by scanning from outside.

response.prompt: Create a triage checklist for a possibly compromised Zyxel GS1900 switch exposed to the internet. Cover checking unknown processes or files, unexpected outbound connections, changed admin accounts, and how to preserve evidence before factory reset. Mention Jitterly and Sixzut malware families. Keep to 10 steps.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to turn the published malware details into a triage checklist for network engineers. They get steps to check for unexpected processes, outbound connections and config changes, to review before use.
response.title: Compromise indicator checklist

response.text: Schedule a weekly job that checks your external attack surface data for Zyxel switch web interfaces and opens a ticket for any hit. The analyst receives the IP, owner and last seen date. Escalate hits unpatched after seven days.
response.title: Weekly external exposure scan

response.text: Create a playbook that lists Check Point gateways and management servers with their Take levels, flags those below the fixed releases and creates a patch ticket per device. It also queues a review of web shells and new local accounts on flagged hosts. Patch windows need owner approval.
response.title: Gateway patch and hunt

response.text: Write an automation that gathers admin login history, recent web server file changes and the socket permission state from affected gateways via your approved remote command integration. Analysts receive one evidence bundle per device for the investigation. Run it only on hosts the analyst selects.
response.title: Collect gateway evidence

response.prompt: This Check Point Gaia flaw (CVE-2026-123039) needs local code execution first and was reportedly seen after PHP2Shell web shell attacks. List 8 hunt hypotheses for the initial foothold and post-root activity on Check Point gateways, with the log source for each. Avoid inventing indicators.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to suggest hunt hypotheses for the foothold that precedes this local escalation. The analyst gets ideas to check in firewall and web logs, to be reviewed before use.
response.title: Post-access hunt hypotheses

response.text: If patching must wait, stop the dynamic_server process as Check Point documents and restrict management-plane access. This removes the escalation path without custom code. Note it also disables Dynamic CLI commands.
response.title: Apply vendor mitigation first

articles.summary: A root-run DynamicCLI daemon accepts commands on a world-writable socket without authentication, so a local user can gain root. Check Point saw exploitation against a couple of dozen customers, reportedly after initial access in PHP2Shell attacks. CISA added it to KEV on 13 November with a 16 November deadline; fixed Jumbo hotfix takes exist.
